# XLSX creation, editing, and analysis

| Task | Approach |
|---|---|
| Create or edit with formulas/formatting | `openpyxl` — see gotchas below |
| Bulk data in or out | `pandas` (`read_excel`, `to_excel`) |
| Quick look at a sheet | `markitdown file.xlsx` — `## SheetName` per sheet; reads `.xlsm` too. No cell coordinates, so don't plan edits from it |
| Read a model (formulas *and* values) | two `load_workbook` passes — see gotchas |

> `openpyxl`, `pandas`, and `markitdown` are preinstalled — do not run `pip install` first; write the script and import directly. Only if an import fails (or the `markitdown` command is missing): `pip install` the missing package.

> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.

## Requirements for every output

- Professional font (Arial, Times New Roman) throughout, unless the user says otherwise.
- Zero formula errors. Never ship while `recalc.py` reports `errors_found`. If you think an error predates you, prove it: load the *original* with `data_only=True` and look at that cell. An error you introduced looks exactly like one you inherited.
- Use formulas, never hardcoded results. Write `sheet['B10'] = '=SUM(B2:B9)'`, not the Python-computed total. The sheet must recalculate when its inputs change.
- Follow the user's spec literally. Exact tab names, exact column headers, and the formula they spelled out. A redesign that computes something else fails, however elegant.
- Document every assumption and hardcoded number where the reader will see it — a cell comment, or an adjacent cell at a table's end. Cite a real source when one exists (`Source: Company 10-K, FY2024, Page 45, Revenue Note, [SEC EDGAR URL]`); when the number came from the user, say so plainly.
- A workbook *you create* for someone to fill in needs a short legend naming which cells to edit, and one example row of realistic values showing the expected format. Never add such a row to a file you were asked to edit.
- Editing an existing file: match its conventions exactly. They override every guideline here. Find its designated input cells first — a distinct font color, fill, or shading marks them — write only there, and leave every existing formula untouched.

## Recalculate (mandatory whenever the file contains formulas)

openpyxl writes formulas as strings with no cached values. Until you recalculate, every
formula cell reads back as `None` to anything reading cached values — `pandas`,
`load_workbook(data_only=True)`, and most previewers.

```bash
python scripts/recalc.py output.xlsx [timeout_seconds] # default 30
```

LibreOffice computes every formula, the file is rewritten in place, and you get JSON:
`status` (`success` | `errors_found`), `total_formulas`, `total_errors`, and an
`error_summary` naming up to 100 cells per error type (`locations_truncated` says how many it
withheld — trust `total_errors`, not the length of the list). Fix what it names and run it
again. JSON with an `error` key instead of a `status` means nothing was recalculated, and
only that case exits non-zero — `errors_found` exits 0, so never treat a clean exit as a clean
workbook.

A green recalc proves your formulas *evaluate*, not that they are *right*. An off-by-one
range or a reference to the wrong row yields a clean, error-free file with wrong numbers.
Write 2–3 formulas first and check they pull the values you expect, before building out a grid.

A workbook that links to another file loses those links if you re-save it with openpyxl and
then recalculate. Such a formula reads `='[1]Returns Analysis'!$B$2` — the `[1]` is an index
into the workbook's external-reference list, naming a *separate file on disk*, not a sheet.
That file is rarely present here, so the cell's cached value is the only thing holding its
data. openpyxl strips that value on save; LibreOffice then has to resolve the reference for
real, fails, writes `#NAME?`, and deletes every link. `recalc.py` refuses to run in that state
— copy those cells' values out of the original before you save over them (`--force` overrides,
and accepts the loss).

## Choosing formulas that survive verification

LibreOffice implements fewer functions than Excel, and one it cannot evaluate becomes a
literal `#NAME?` baked into the file you deliver.

- Prefer Excel-2007-era functions — `SUMIFS`, `INDEX`, `MATCH`, `IFERROR`, `SUMPRODUCT` — which need no prefix.
- Six post-2007 functions work, but only with an `_xlfn.` prefix, because openpyxl writes your formula into the XML verbatim and Excel stores post-2007 names prefixed (its UI hides the prefix): `_xlfn.TEXTJOIN`, `_xlfn.CONCAT`, `_xlfn.IFS`, `_xlfn.SWITCH`, `_xlfn.MAXIFS`, `_xlfn.MINIFS`. Written bare, each yields `#NAME?`.
- Never use `XLOOKUP`, `XMATCH`, `SORT`, `FILTER`, `UNIQUE`, or `SEQUENCE`. The runtime's LibreOffice cannot evaluate them under *any* prefix. Newer builds do evaluate them, but they are spilling array functions and an openpyxl-written file has no spill metadata, so only the top-left cell of the range gets a value — and `recalc.py` reports `total_errors: 0` on the truncated result. Use `INDEX`/`MATCH` for lookups, and sort, filter, and de-duplicate in Python before writing the cells.
- A formula LibreOffice could not parse is written back lowercased — a quick tell beside a `#NAME?`.

## openpyxl gotchas

- Reading a model takes two loads. `data_only=True` yields cached values with the formulas gone; the default yields formula strings with no values. One pass cannot give you both.
- `data_only=True` is destructive if you save. That workbook has no formulas left, so saving replaces every one with a literal — permanently.
- `data_only=True` on a file openpyxl just wrote returns `None` everywhere — run `recalc.py` first. (A formula whose result is `""` also reads back as `None`.)
- Merged cells: write the top-left anchor only. Every other cell in the range is a `MergedCell` whose `.value` is read-only.
- `.xlsm` loses its macros unless you pass `keep_vba=True` to `load_workbook`.
- A sheet name containing a space must be quoted in a cross-sheet reference: `='Assumptions Inputs'!$B$5`. Unquoted, it evaluates to `#VALUE!`.

## Financial models

Unless the user says otherwise, or the existing file already does something else.

Color: blue text (`0,0,255`) for hardcoded inputs and scenario levers · black for formulas ·
green (`0,128,0`) for links to another sheet · red (`255,0,0`) for links to another file ·
yellow fill (`255,255,0`) for key assumptions and cells the user should fill in.

Numbers: currency `$#,##0`, with the unit named in the header (`Revenue ($mm)`) · zeros
render as `-`, including in percentages (`$#,##0;($#,##0);-`) · negatives in parentheses ·
percentages `0.0%`, stored as fractions (`0.15` renders `15.0%`; storing `15` renders
`1500.0%`) · valuation multiples `0.0x` · years as text (`"2024"`, never `2,024`).

Structure: every assumption in its own labeled cell, referenced by the formulas that use it
(`=B5*(1+$B$6)`, never `=B5*1.05`) · formulas consistent across every projection period, since a
lone edited cell mid-row is the commonest silent error · guard denominators that can be zero.

## Dependencies

`openpyxl`, `pandas`, `markitdown` (pip, preinstalled — install only if an import fails or the command is missing) · LibreOffice (`soffice`, auto-configured for sandboxed environments via `scripts/office/soffice.py`)

## PART 1 — PER SHEET

### 07 Product Standards (48r × 34c)
- Purpose: Anchor rate/economics table per product family: Units/Batch, Batches/Shift, Planned Units/Day-Week, crew, Base Weekly Demand, Monthly Growth %, ASP, material/packaging cost, starting FG, safety-stock weeks, lab/packaging/shipping lead days, plus 10 leadership-routing columns (Z–AH).

Only Regular Pre-Rolls has real rates (C8=6,800 units/batch, D8=2 batches/shift, E8=1 shift → G8=13,600/day, H8=68,000/week, crew J8=4). The other 3 families are all zeros. Every economic input is zero for all 4 rows — ASP (M), material cost (N), packaging cost (O), Base Weekly Demand (K), Monthly Growth % (L), starting FG (P), lab lead days (S). Safety stock Q=2 weeks everywhere (default).
- Defects: Responsible Department (X5:X8) empty → cached AG5:AG8 = "DEPARTMENT REQUIRED" and AH=0; entire leadership block (Z–AH) resolves to "INPUT REQUIRED" via IFERROR-masked INDEX/MATCH to 'Department Leadership Matrix'. Column-doc block (rows 14–48) is auto-generated boilerplate that misdescribes columns (e.g., A20 "Batches/Day … the applicable operating date or period"). ### 11 Sales &amp; Demand (444r × 34c)
- Purpose: Single source of truth for forecasts + firm orders: Demand ID, Type, Customer, Channel, order/ship dates, Family, SKU, units, price, discount, revenue, contribution, OTIF/risk, Linked Work Order.
- DATA REALITY: 0% — zero real demand records. 400 template rows (5–404) all identical: B="Forecast", K/L/N/O=0, T="Normal", U="Open"; no customer, SKU, date, or price anywhere. The company's demand signal does not exist in the workbook.
- Formula logic is live: M=MAX(K−L,0), P=N*(1−O), Q=K*P, S=Q−R, OTIF text in V, and R5 = K5*SUMIF('Product Standards'!$A$5:$A$8,…) — material+packaging cost lookup hard-bound to the 4-family table (rows 5:8 only). X hardcodes "Sales" as responsible dept.
- Defects: cost lookup silently returns $0 for any family not in Product Standards A5:A8 → contribution S overstated to 100% of revenue. No demand-type granularity (no month/period column — demand is dated only by ship dates).

### 16 Manufacturing Schedule (573r × 63c)
- Purpose: One row per work-order stage: WO, Sales Demand ID link, family/SKU/batch/lot, sequence/stage/dept, planned vs actual dates &amp; units, labor (Employee 1–5, Y=COUNTA headcount, Z=Y*Controls!$B$12 available hours, utilization AB), material-ready, testing, FG release, ship, Vincent Approval (AL), Approved Material Qty (AM), Release to Manufacture (AN), shift fields (AZ–BF), Monday.com sync stubs (BG:BK — Board/Group/Item ID, Last Synced, Sync Status).
- DATA REALITY: 0% — zero real work orders. 500 slots (rows 5–504) all template: F/M/N/P/Q/S=0, AC="No", AD="Yes", AJ="Planned". The Monday.com columns exist but have never synced.

### 20 Weekly Production &amp; FG (961r × 27c)
- Purpose: Weekly S&amp;OP engine: every week Aug 2026 → Dec 2030 × 4 families (~930 rows). D/E demand SUMIFS from Sales Demand ($M$5:$M$404 by requested-ship week), F=MAX(D+E, base weekly demand), G planned production = working days × Product Standards units/day, H actual FG from Manufacturing Schedule ($P$5:$P$504), I/J FG roll-forward (I6=J5), K safety target, L shortage, M weeks cover, N/O revenue &amp; variable cost, P alert.
- DATA REALITY: formulas 100% live, inputs ~0%. All demand/revenue/cost columns compute 0. Working Days C correctly pulls holidays from Planning Calendar (C25=3 for Christmas week 2026-12-21; normal weeks=5).
- Hard fact / headline defect: phantom inventory. Regular Pre-Rolls produces 68,000/wk with zero demand, so ending FG (J) compounds: J705=530,400 by 2026-09-21; J723=1,700,000 by 2027-01-25; J777=5,372,000 by 2028-02-07; ~15M+ by 2030 — and every alert cell P says "OK." ## PART 2 — DOMAIN SYNTHESIS

### The one-sentence diagnosis
The planning architecture is genuinely well-designed (demand → weekly S&amp;OP → work orders → replenishment triggers → Vincent approval → Monday.com sync), but it is an engine with no fuel: 0 demand records (11), 0 SKUs (28), 0 BOMs (25), 0 equipment (24), 0 work orders (16), economics all zero (07) — while the real numbers that should populate them sit un-reviewed in quarantine (50: ~770 rows, 0 reviewed) and un-reconciled in the legacy snapshot (72).

### TOP GAPS (missing entirely for a ~500-SKU cannabis manufacturer)
1. No SKU dimension in planning. Demand (11), weekly plan (20), and standards (07) operate on 4 product *families*; the 500-SKU master (28) and 20-category portfolio (29) never connect to weekly production. There is no family→category→SKU hierarchy or allocation logic anywhere.
2. No demand input pipeline. Nothing imports POS/dispensary sell-through, distributor orders, or Metrc transfer history; Avg Weekly Demand (28 S) is a manual field. No statistical forecast, no seasonality (4/20, holidays), no forecast-vs-actual accuracy tracking.
3. No multi-level BOM / co-product model. Extraction reality in sheet 50 (biomass → crude 29% → diamonds 35% + remaining crude 65%; hash → rosin 81%) cannot be represented in 25's single-level per-unit BOM. No bulk-intermediate stage (oil, hash, milled flower) between cultivation output and finished SKUs.
4. No material/biomass constraint. Weekly plan G is rate × days; nothing checks whether flower/trim/oil supply exists (Cultivation categories exist in 29 but no harvest plan feeds 20 or 16).
5. No finite-capacity scheduling. Equipment (24) is disconnected from the schedule (16); labor (max 5 employees/row) and machines are never netted against the weekly plan; no bottleneck or load-vs-capacity view by week.
6. No testing/compliance pipeline in the flow. Lab lead days exist as columns (07 S, 16 AD/AE) but no COA tracking, batch-hold aging, retest loop, or Metrc tag/manifest linkage — mandatory for a Metrc-regulated operator.
7. No actuals capture loop. Every "Actual" column in 16/20/72 is empty and there is no mechanism (import or form) to record daily output — variance, OEE, % of plan are permanently blank.
8. No expiry/freshness or lot-aging logic in replenishment (28) — cannabis FG has shelf life and testing windows; FIFO/expiry is unmodeled.
9. No scenario/what-if layer — one deterministic plan to 2030; no price, yield, or demand sensitivity despite 50 containing three flower-price scenarios ($741/$970/$1,133).
10. No data-governance state machine — 50 and 72 both define review workflows (owner/status/decision) that have never advanced a single row; nothing forces or tracks the quarantine→approved→propagated transition.

### TOP IMPROVEMENTS (highest-impact fixes to what exists)
1. Fix the "OK" blind spot in 20 P (biggest silent-failure risk): alert should test absolute FG (J) against a cap, not only weeks-cover M which blanks at zero demand — today 15M phantom pre-rolls by 2030 read "OK" (20 J705→J777 progression).
2. Populate Product Standards economics from sheet 50 — ASP, material, packaging cost per family are the multipliers for every revenue/margin cell in 11 and 20; all are 0. The numbers exist (e.g., pre-roll $3.20 materials+labor, $0.33+$1.862 packaging, $2.741 price/joint).
3. Unbind the 4-row SUMIF anchor: every lookup hard-codes 'Product Standards'!$A$5:$A$8 (11 R5; 20 F/G/I/K/N/O). Adding a 5th family (Concentrates, Solventless — already in 29) silently computes $0 cost/0 capacity. Convert to a structured table / dynamic range and add an "unmatched family" error trap.
4. Resolve sheet 50's conflicts before propagation: Extraction Labor 50 vs 140; diamonds-from-oil 35% vs 75% (A42 vs A285); 5 different bubble-hash yields; the DIV/0 vape margin (A369) and −21.4% margin line (A747). Assign the named owners (Bert, Kyle, Josh) rows, fill G (target field), and burn down the 770-row review queue.
5. Reconcile 72 → 07/20: the H2O process runs a 4-day week (50 A411) but everything downstream assumes 5 (07 H=G*5; 24 H=5); the vape and flower/infused daily schedules need planned units the way Regular Pre-Rolls has them (13,600/day).
6. Seed the SKU Master (28) and set Target Active SKUs (29 C) — the entire trigger/approval engine and the portfolio scorecard are dead until then; today 13 of 20 categories show zero gap because targets are blank, which reads as "on plan."
7. Name the equipment (24) and replace the 100%-OEE default with measured values; link work-center to 16 rows so utilization means something.
8. Replace the auto-generated column documentation (every sheet's bottom block) — many descriptions are wrong for their columns (e.g., 29 A53 describes "Target Active SKUs" as a traceability identifier), which will mislead new staff and any app-migration mapping.
9. Surface, don't mask, lookup failures: the universal IFERROR→"INPUT REQUIRED"/blank pattern hides broken cross-references (07 Z:AH, 24 T:AB); add a visible error-count banner per sheet.
10. Give Controls!$B$32 one meaning — it is simultaneously the reorder cover-weeks (28 U) and half the excess-capital threshold (20 P); split into named constants.

### FEATURES / FUNCTIONS / TOOLS TO ADD

(a) Within Excel / Google Sheets (near-term)
- Data-completeness dashboard: per-sheet % populated, count of "INPUT REQUIRED"/"REVIEW REQUIRED"/"Reconcile Before Use" cells, with owner names — makes the fuel-gap visible to the owner in one screen (right now it takes a forensic audit).
- Import burn-down tracker for 50/72: pivot of rows by owner × status; conditional formatting aging on Review Date; a "Propagate" macro/Apps Script that writes an approved value into its target cell (F+G) and stamps J/K/L.
- SKU ID scheme + validation: structured SKU code (DEPT-CAT-BRAND-SIZE-####), data-validation dropdowns bound to 29's category list, duplicate detection, and cross-sheet name canonicalization (see inconsistencies below).
- SKU-level demand cube: a proper demand table (SKU × week) feeding both 20 (aggregated to family) and 28 S (avg weekly demand) — one demand number, two consumers, no manual re-typing.
- Capacity-check column in 20: planned production G vs Σ effective weekly units from 24 by department; flag weeks where plan &gt; capacity.
- Safety-stock and EXCESS alerts driven by targets that exist: wire 29 F (target minimum units) into 20 K / 28 K as the floor instead of the zeroed Product-Standards path.
- Scenario switcher: the three flower-price tiers already imported (741/970/1,133) as a dropdown driving 07 ASP → instant margin sensitivity.
- Holiday-aware everywhere: 72's holiday calendar is correct and 20 already reads Planning Calendar; extend the same working-days logic to 24 (H=5 hardcoded) and 16 date math.

(b) Software / app + Monday.com level (the destination)
- Metrc integration as the actuals backbone: pull packages, harvests, transfers, and lab results nightly → auto-fill 16 P (actual units), 20 H, 28 N/O (on-hand/testing hold), and lot traceability that 25 N promises. This single integration eliminates the empty-actuals problem permanently.
- Monday.com two-way sync (the stubs exist — 16 BG:BK): work orders as items, stages as subitems/groups, status mirroring both ways, Last Synced/Sync Status enforcement, and Vincent's approval (16 AL, 28 Y/AA) as a Monday approval column with audit trail instead of a typed cell.
- Replenishment service: recompute 28's trigger logic (BUILD NOW/PLAN BUILD, P0/P1) on live inventory + rolling demand; push P0s to a Monday "Build Queue" board; require approval before a WO is generated in 16 — the workbook's exact intended workflow, made event-driven.
- Demand forecasting module: sell-through ingestion (dispensary POS/distributor EDI/CSV), 13-week rolling forecast per SKU with seasonality and promo flags, forecast-accuracy KPI (MAPE) — replacing the 400 empty forecast rows.
- Multi-level BOM engine with co-products: biomass → crude (29%) → diamonds (35%) + remainder; hash → rosin (81%); yield-versioned recipes; automatic bulk-intermediate requirements planning (MRP) from the FG plan back to flower/trim purchase or harvest needs, priced with 50's real costs.
- Finite scheduler: allocate WOs to work centers (24) and crews (16 T:X) against shift calendars with changeover/downtime; flag overloads; publish the daily plan to Monday and to a shop-floor tablet view that captures actual batches/units (closing 72's empty N/O loop).
- Compliance/testing tracker: COA status per lot, testing-hold aging (28 O), retest workflow, and release gating of FG (16 AF/AG) tied to lab results.
- Import/quarantine service: generalize sheet 50 into a standing pipeline — any source workbook lands as staged key/value rows with owner assignment, diff-vs-current-standard, one-click approve-and-propagate, full audit log. (The current tab proves the pattern; it just has no workflow engine behind it.)
- Alerting with no blind spots: absolute-inventory caps, demand=0-but-production&gt;0 detectors, unmatched-family/SKU lookups, negative-margin SKUs (50 already imported one at −21.4%) — pushed to Monday/Slack rather than living as a cell color.

### CROSS-SHEET INCONSISTENCIES (observed, cited)
1. Family-name drift: 07/20/29 use "Flower 3.5g"; 72 B5 uses "3.5g Flower". Any future join between the legacy snapshot and the planning chain mismatches on the primary key.
2. 4 families vs 20 categories vs 500 SKUs: 07 defines 4 (A5:A8); 29 defines 20 categories incl. Cultivation grades, Concentrates, Solventless, Hydrocarbon, Pre-Ground, Specialty/Economy lines; 28 provisions 500 SKUs. The planning formulas (11 R5; 20 F/G/I/K/N/O) only recognize the 4 — everything else would flow through at $0 cost and 0 capacity with no error.
3. Consistency that does hold: 72's Regular Pre-Rolls plan (R=6,800 × S=2 × T=1 = 13,600/day, row 516) exactly matches 07 row 8 (C8/D8/E8 → G8) and 20's computed 68,000/week (G705) — the one populated thread is internally coherent end-to-end.
4. Work-week conflict: 50 A411 (H2O IN_OUT) says 4 workdays/week; 07 H=G*5, 24 H=5, and 20's calendar assume 5-day weeks (holidays excepted).
5. Yield conflicts inside the import: diamonds-from-oil 35% (50 A42) vs 75% (50 A285); extraction labor $50 (A16) vs $140 (A41); three run sizes (6,810/27,240/20,430g) with process context lost — unresolvable downstream until reviewed.
6. Range wiring is correct: 20 D/E → 'Sales Demand'!$M$5:$M$404 matches 11's 400 slots; 20 H → 'Manufacturing Schedule'!$P$5:$P$504 matches 16's 500 slots; 29's COUNTIFS/SUMIFS → 'SKU Master Replenishment' $5:$504 matches 28. The plumbing agrees; only the fixed $A$5:$A$8 anchor (item 2) and naming (item 1) are fragile.
7. Safety stock defined twice, effective nowhere: 07 Q=2 weeks × zero base demand → 20 K=0; 29 F minimums (120/480/72/48/48/2,000/500) are the only real inventory floors but nothing in 20 or 28 reads them.
8. Approval workflow split across sheets with no shared state: Vincent approval fields exist independently in 16 (AL/AM/AN) and 28 (Y/Z/AA) with no linkage; an approved build in 28 does not create or reference a WO in 16 except via the manual Linked Work Order text column (28 AB / 11 W).
9. Error hygiene: zero cached #REF!/#DIV/0!/#N/A in all 10 sheets — but only because IFERROR blankets every lookup; the one genuine error is preserved as imported text (50 D369 "SOURCE FORMULA ERROR — DIVIDE BY ZERO") plus a legacy negative margin (50 A747, −21.38%) that no one has dispositioned.

Bottom line for the owner: nothing structural is missing from the *design* of the demand-to-production chain — what is missing is (1) the data (SKUs, demand, BOMs, equipment: all 0%), (2) the review muscle to move 770 quarantined real numbers into the standards tables, (3) SKU-level granularity connecting the 500-SKU ambition to family-level planning, and (4) alerting that cannot show "OK" while the model builds 15 million unsellable pre-rolls. The highest-leverage app features are Metrc-driven actuals, the replenishment→approval→Monday work-order loop the columns already anticipate, and a real demand pipeline.</result>

## PART 2 — DOMAIN SYNTHESIS

State in one line: real payroll history (1 sheet, 21 people, 4 weeks) + a well-designed but ~85% empty control shell; the two operational engines (Time &amp; Attendance, Schedule Board) hold zero records, and the hiring/budget math is corrupted by a column-shift bug and string-matching failures that together misstate the labor plan by roughly $16K/week of existing wages and ~11 phantom hires.

### TOP GAPS (missing entirely)
1. No actual time capture. 750-row T&amp;A ledger has zero punches; payroll "history" is 4 static weeks ending 7/26/2026, 8+ days stale vs the 8/3 planning week. No feed from any timeclock/POS/payroll system (no import tab, no mapping).
2. No PTO/sick/leave subsystem. PTO is only a note in Source Payroll A2 ("remain included"); no accrual balances, requests, approvals, or absence calendar; T&amp;A has an Exception column but no absence codes.
3. No shift catalog or coverage rules. "Shift" is free text; no defined shift times, min-staffing per room/stage, weekend/holiday policy (Planning Calendar referenced but weekly budget hardcodes ÷5).
4. No compliance layer for a Metrc cannabis workforce: no badge/agent-card numbers or expiry tracking, no training/certification matrix (extraction safety, food handling), no per-employee Metrc permissions — nothing links people to regulated activities.
5. No labor-cost-to-product linkage. Schedule Board has Work Order/SKU columns but nothing computes actual labor $ per batch/SKU; Weekly Dept Schedule only budgets at dept level.
6. No employee lifecycle: hire/term dates, onboarding checklist, I-9/W-4 status, rate-change history (60's Effective/End dates empty), review dates. Inactives are just rows flagged "Inactive".
7. No overtime governance loop: OT is computed from *target* hours (Roster X formula uses S, not actual R), so real OT (Terio 41.13 avg, F23 sheet 01) is never priced or alerted.
8. No backup/succession anywhere: every Escalation/Backup cell in 27, 61, 63 is "INPUT REQUIRED"; Vincent's approval bottleneck (27!I9) has no deputy.
9. No totals/dashboard on the leadership budget (62 lacks a total row; the ~$31.8K/wk hierarchy requirement appears nowhere as a number).
10. No skills/cross-training matrix despite a FLOAT-HR tier (60!A10) built explicitly for cross-trained reassignment.

### TOP IMPROVEMENTS (fix what exists)
1. Repair the Workforce Roster AA/AB/AC column shift (AA should be `Z×52`, AB `AP×G`, AC `AP×J`) and repoint Department Budget K — this single fix restores the $16,440/wk existing wage bill into every budget number.
2. Force a full recalculation and re-save; then reconcile Department Budget totals (F13 640→920, K13, N6/N10 ghosts). Add a self-check row `=IF(F13&lt;&gt;SUM(F5:F12),"STALE","OK")`.
3. Replace exact-string role/dept matching with controlled dropdowns from a single Departments/Roles reference table (canonical lists; kill "Quality/Compliance" vs "Quality &amp; Testing", "Trimmer/Trimmers", "Flower &amp; Specialty Equipment"). This alone deletes ~11 phantom hires from Position Plan.
4. Fix the placeholder-evasion bug: change coverage checks from `=“INPUT REQUIRED”` equality to `ISNUMBER(SEARCH("INPUT REQUIRED",cell))` or require a match against the roster name list — Finance would correctly flip to HEAD REQUIRED (61!AF18, 63!X22).
5. Filter LCHK-09 (and any `"&lt;&gt;"` COUNTIFS) to rows where the anchor cell has length &gt;0, cutting 91 → 5 real exceptions.
6. Enter the missing decisions the model is starving for: 8 dept heads, assistant/supervisor rates (&gt;$22 per M6/M7), 4 P0 hires (Planner, QA Coordinator, Sales owner, S&amp;OP owner), and named backups.
7. Base pay/OT on actual hours: wage formula should use MAX(actual, scheduled) or a payroll-period actuals column, and flag S22-style 50-hour targets explicitly.
8. Normalize IDs: store Reports-To as text "00000002" matching A-col; use Employee ID (not name) in Schedule Board overlap keys.
9. Make weekday budget calendar-aware (`÷ operating days from Planning Calendar` instead of ÷5) and give cultivation a 7-day stage pattern in 63 (R=7).
10. Add `if_empty` ("no rows") to all FILTER views and set default selectors to the Controls week (B23), not Saturday 8/1.

Vinny · 2026-08-04 20:20
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

Honor what's already there Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

Ground it in the subject. If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

Pair typefaces Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

Choose neutrals, don't default to them. A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

Design both themes. The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` and `:root[data-theme="light"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.

Let layout do the spacing. Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

Avoid AI-generated design AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

Build cleanly Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

CSS rules When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

Writing the copy Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

Structure is information Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

When it's a UI, not a document A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- Color: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- Type: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- Layout: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

Principles

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment.
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated.
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.
